idiom_name: Thread.new workers over a Thread::Queue (Ractor or processes for CPU parallelism)
implementation_notes: The local idiom is a fixed set of Thread.new workers popping from a Thread::Queue - the queue class implements all the required locking semantics, so the master only pushes work items and joins at the end, and the partial results return through a second queue or a per-task slot. CRuby threads run under the GVL, so this gives concurrency (overlapped I/O) but not parallel Ruby bytecode: CPU-bound decomposition must use Ractor (each Ractor holds its own GVL and shares only shareable objects, which forces value-style task and result payloads) or process-based workers. async-style libraries fit the I/O-bound case without threads.
pitfalls: The GVL means Thread workers do not give CPU parallelism; use Ractor or forked processes for CPU-bound subtasks.
A worker thread that raises dies silently unless Thread.report_on_exception/abort_on_exception is set, and the master then waits in join forever.
Ractor payloads must be shareable or moved (deep clone or transfer); mutable globals and unshareable objects cannot cross the boundary.
